newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria stocks rise to new peak, insurers rally.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria stocks rise to new peak, insurers rally.

text.p: Insurance firms joined the ranks of rising stocks on the Nigerian bourse on Wednesday as the index broke through 8000 for the first time, traders said.
The all-share index closed at 8009.50 from 7951.17 on Tuesday.
"Investors currently looking for good investment options are turning to the sector where potential for growth are quite real," said one trader.
Traders also attributed the new interest to the relatively low price of insurance stocks compared to the market leaders.
AIICO Insurance, the leading stock in the sector, closed three kobo up at 13.90 naira.
Prestige Assurance was 5.32 naira, two kobo higher and UNIC rose three kobo to 4.90 naira.
Demand for blue chip stocks remained strong and further gains were seen.
Coca-Cola bottler, the Nigerian Bottling Company climbed to 47.60 naira, 60 kobo up, followed by Cadbury, up 30 kobo at 35.30 naira.
Conglomerates PZ PZIN.LG and Lever Brothers were 30 kobo stronger at 24.30 naira and 22.80 naira, respectively, while UAC finished 20 kobo up at 12.20 naira.
Bank shares maintained their positive movement, led by First Bank with a 30 kobo gain to 15.90 naira.
Guinness and Nigerian Breweries climbed 20 kobo each to 7.60 naira and 16.60 naira, respectively.
"It shows the excess volumes have been effectively mopped up," said one trader.
But it was not the case for falling Benue Cement Company which closed at 5.66 naira, down 24 kobo.
West African Portland Cement Company maintained its steady rise, closing 20 kobo up at 61.60 naira. Ashaka Cement also edged up by five kobo to 13.65 naira.
Textile group Afprint dropped three kobo to 2.25 naira. Dealers said it would drop more due to sell pressures after the government lowered tarrifs on imported textiles.
